description: Original editorial summaries of Steiner's historically attributed teachings. No copied lecture bodies. All nontrivial doctrinal cards resolve to exact dated primary-source links in their guide. Scientific anatomical facts are visually distinguished from esoteric assertions.

guides.title: The heart
guides.subtitle: Warmth · rhythm · inward experience
guides.one_liner: In Steiner's teachings the heart is discussed as a developing disposition, a rhythmic organization and an image of spiritual inwardness.
guides.intro: Explore the heart through several distinct settings: early planetary evolution, the rhythm of present bodily life, a claimed inward sense, and images of conscience. They should not be merged into one physical explanation.

quick_takeaways.title: Its beginnings are not modern anatomy
quick_takeaways.body: Steiner's Old Saturn account concerns the first disposition of a heart, not a muscular organ as it exists today.

quick_takeaways.title: The living organism is relational
quick_takeaways.body: A medical lecture interprets rhythm through the contrasting influences of head and metabolism.

quick_takeaways.title: Spiritually interpreted, not clinically established
quick_takeaways.body: Steiner also gives the heart inward-sense and conscience meanings, which are historical esoteric claims.

body.note: The heart is located in the chest between the lungs, somewhat left of the midline. Anatomically it pumps blood through the circulatory system. The spiritual claims discussed in the remaining layers are not established physiological explanations.

cards.title: Location and circulation
cards.body: The heart lies in the thorax and pumps blood through the body. This is general anatomical orientation, distinct from Steiner's esoteric explanations.

cards.title: Rhythm as a whole-body theme
cards.body: Steiner describes rhythmic balancing in relation to head and metabolic processes, not simply as a local chest matter.

cards.title: Heart and lungs
cards.body: A 1922 medical lecture discusses heart–lung activity in connection with the etheric organization. Treat this as Steiner's interpretation, not modern mechanism.

interpretation.intro: The following diagrams are categories of explanation, not four literal anatomical layers. Some describe the human members; others are organ analogies.

cards.title: Rhythmic organization
cards.body: The rhythmic organization is described as arising amid head and metabolic influences.

cards.title: Etheric relation
cards.body: The heart–lung discussion places activity in relation to etheric organization; the source does not license an exclusive spiritual organ-builder.

cards.title: Astral and I interpretation
cards.body: Steiner characterizes the heart as a purported inward organ sensing astral and I-related activity.

cards.title: Conscience and future life
cards.body: Steiner links the heart's surface and interior to images of conscience and karmic dispositions. These are historical spiritual assertions.

evolution.lead: A context map, not a physically validated evolutionary timeline. Earth's recapitulation is not the same as the original Old Saturn embodiment.

timeline.title: First heart disposition
timeline.body: A rudimentary heart organization is attributed to the earliest cosmic conditions; this is not a present-day anatomical heart.

timeline.title: A warmth-centered structure
timeline.body: Steiner describes branching warmth and a heart disposition while Earth repeats earlier conditions, distinguishing it from the mature organ.

timeline.title: Rhythm and inward significance
timeline.body: Later lectures treat rhythm, purported inner sensing and conscience through separate organ interpretive frameworks.

timeline.title: Detailed heart sequence still open
timeline.body: The present dossier does not establish a fully sourced organ-specific account for every future planetary condition.

compare.conclusion: These have different temporal references. Neither dates the modern physical heart to a warmth-only state.

agencies.intro: A named being's stage, donation, ordering or preservation activity is not necessarily an exclusive claim that it built the present organ.

rows.caveat: Do not collapse Thrones, Cherubim and Seraphim into a single builder.

rows.agent: Not specified as one exclusive rank
rows.caveat: No unique hierarchy assigned to every rhythmic activity.
Not a claim of clinical detection by the heart.

connections.intro: Tap a relationship for its explanation and original source. Different kinds of connections should not be interpreted as identical causal mechanisms.

nodes.label: Blood
nodes.detail: The heart belongs to the circulation; Steiner interprets rhythm and life activity in other registers.

nodes.label: Warmth
nodes.detail: GA 205 links the heart with a warmth element in Steiner's esoteric account.

nodes.label: Rhythm
nodes.detail: Rhythmic organization is described in relation to opposing bodily poles.

nodes.label: Conscience
nodes.detail: The heart is used to express feelings of conscience and their purported spiritual reflection.

nodes.label: Inner sense
nodes.detail: A 1924 lecture describes an inner sense of astral and I-related processes.

questions.title: Who acts at each evolutionary stage?
questions.body: The hierarchy comparisons need to distinguish named actors, kind of action and stage. No exclusive modern-heart builder is established.

questions.title: How should Sun symbolism be compared?
questions.body: Present solar correspondence and primordial genesis must remain separate until directly reconciled with passages in their full context.

questions.title: What is incomplete?
questions.body: The first-pass English readings and selected German comparisons do not yet constitute exhaustive bilingual, independent verification.

questions.title: Historical medical error
questions.body: Steiner's denial that the heart pumps blood is contrary to established cardiovascular physiology. This is a historical source claim, not advice.

sources.context: Named hierarchy roles, Old Saturn; requires role distinction

guides.title: The liver
guides.subtitle: Nourishment · will · planetary analogy
guides.one_liner: Steiner associates the liver with food processes, a Jupiter analogy, the developing head and forms of willing.
guides.intro: Liver teachings in different lectures belong to different explanatory contexts. A planetary metaphor, an inward-sense idea, childhood development and an elemental correspondence are not interchangeable facts.

quick_takeaways.title: Jupiter is a correspondence
quick_takeaways.body: In GA 128 Steiner provisionally invokes an inner Jupiter relationship; this does not date the organ's physical creation.

quick_takeaways.title: Nourishment is central
quick_takeaways.body: A 1924 lecture describes a purported inward sense for the value of food, distinct from the modern biochemical role of the liver.

quick_takeaways.title: Head and will are separate themes
quick_takeaways.body: Medical and curative-education lectures discuss liver–gall/head relations and the child's intentions becoming movement.

body.note: The liver is in the upper right abdomen beneath the diaphragm. Modern anatomy describes it as performing metabolic, synthetic, detoxification and bile-producing functions. This general orientation is different from Steiner's attributed claims.

cards.title: Position and physiology
cards.body: The liver lies mainly under the right rib cage; it processes nutrients, synthesizes proteins and makes bile. This is ordinary anatomy.

cards.title: Liver versus liver–gall system
cards.body: Some of Steiner's statements refer to the combined liver–gall organization. The Atlas keeps that scope distinct from liver-only claims.

cards.title: Nourishment in Steiner's account
cards.body: GA 128 connects liver, bile and spleen to ascending nutritional processes; GA 316 supplies another inner-sense image.

interpretation.intro: These are different spiritual-scientific interpretations of liver activity; no claim is presented as modern clinical diagnosis.

cards.title: The nourishment account
cards.body: Steiner portrays the liver as a purported inward sense of the value of food.

cards.title: I and liver–gall
cards.body: A 1922 medical discussion links liver–gall, warmth and I organization; do not treat every such statement as liver-alone.

cards.title: Head relationship
cards.body: GA 314 describes childhood head reflection of liver–gall-related influences.

cards.title: Will and movement
cards.body: Steiner proposes an association of the liver with translating intention into movement in a curative-education context.

evolution.lead: These are explanatory settings, not a linear sequence of the liver being formed on Jupiter and then Earth.

timeline.title: Inner Jupiter analogy
timeline.body: GA 128 uses a provisional analogy involving inner Jupiter. It is not an astronomical claim that liver tissue formed on the planet Jupiter.

timeline.title: Nourishment and inner sensing
timeline.body: Steiner discusses nutritive processes and a claimed inward awareness of food value.

timeline.title: Head, will and liver–gall
timeline.body: Distinct lectures treat liver–gall/head reflections and intention becoming movement.

timeline.title: Future brain dispositions
timeline.body: GA 205 links inner organ activity to a claimed future disposition, without proving a complete cosmic liver evolution sequence.

compare.conclusion: Two different relationship types: neither justifies saying Jupiter physically made the liver out of water.

agencies.intro: The sources in this guide do not establish a unique hierarchy whose sole work is to build the finished liver.

rows.agent: Spiritual agents not uniquely identified here
rows.caveat: Correspondence is not a named builder.
The I is a member of the human constitution, not a separate named hierarchy.

rows.agent: Human intention / etheric processes in the lecture
rows.caveat: This remains a historical interpretation, not a cause of movement disorders.

connections.intro: These relationships involve nourishment, symbolism, childhood formation and spiritual interpretations; they cannot be fused into a single diagram of physical causation.

nodes.label: Nourishment
nodes.detail: An inward-sense account and the nutritional activities discussed with bile and spleen.

nodes.label: Jupiter
nodes.detail: The provisional inner Jupiter analogy in GA 128.

nodes.label: Head
nodes.detail: Childhood head reflection and the relation of organs to differentiation.

nodes.label: Will
nodes.detail: A historical association of the liver with intention becoming movement.

nodes.label: Water
nodes.detail: GA 205 gives an elemental water affiliation, distinct from Jupiter.

questions.title: Was the liver formed by particular Saturn beings?
questions.body: Steiner's planetary/cosmic agency descriptions require further original-context comparison. Do not substitute the Jupiter analogy for such a claim.

questions.title: Where does liver–gall differ from liver alone?
questions.body: Several sources describe the broader organ system. The dossier should retain the actual target named in each lecture.

questions.title: Are the medical implications established?
questions.body: No. The liver–will and illness accounts are historical esoteric teachings, not validated explanations of neurological or developmental conditions.

questions.title: What is still pending?
questions.body: Whole-original-German collation, comprehensive cross-volume reconciliation and independent second review remain unfinished.
